2.1: Thus the heavens and the earth were completed, and all their ordered host.
2.2: And on the seventh day God completed His work which He had done, and He rested on the seventh day from all His work which He had done.
2.3: Then God blessed the seventh day and set it apart, because on it He rested from all His work which God had created and made.
2.4: This is the account of the heavens and the earth in their creation, when the LORD God shaped the earth and the heavens.
2.5: Before any shrub of the field was upon the earth, and before any plant of the field had sprung up, the LORD God had not caused rain to fall upon the land, and there was no man to work the soil.
2.6: But a mist would rise from the earth and water the whole surface of the ground.
2.7: Then the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground, breathed life into him, and man became a living soul.
2.8: And the LORD God planted a garden in Eden, to the east, and there He set the man He had formed.
2.9: And out of the ground the LORD God caused every tree to grow that was pleasing to the sight and good for food, including the tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
2.10: Now a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided and became four headwaters.
2.11: The first river is called Pishon; it circles the entire land of Havilah, a land rich with gold.
2.12: The gold of that land is of fine quality; bdellium and onyx stone are also found there.
2.13: The second river is called Gihon; it circles the entire land of Cush.
2.14: The name of the third river is Tigris; it flows east of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
2.15: And the LORD God took the man and placed him in the garden of Eden, to serve it and to watch over it.
2.16: And the LORD God gave command to the man, saying, "You are free to eat from every tree of the garden."
2.17: But from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you must not eat, for in the day you eat from it, you will surely die.
2.18: Then the LORD God said, "It is not good for the man to be alone; I will make a helper who corresponds to him."
2.19: From the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and brought them before Adam to see what he would name them; and each living creature was called by the name Adam gave it.
2.20: So Adam gave names to all the livestock, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam no helper corresponding to him was found.
2.21: So the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and while he slept, He took one from his side and closed up the flesh in its place.
2.22: And the LORD God built the side He had taken from the man into a woman, and He brought her to the man.
2.23: And Adam said, "At last, this is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh. She shall be called Woman, for she was taken from man."
2.24: Therefore a man leaves his father and mother and is joined to his wife, and they become one flesh.
2.25: And the man and his wife were both naked and were not ashamed.
